title: Ironhollow Rising Revisited
premise: Oscar Marchetti, a woman cartographer who maps realms that exist only in rumor, lives in Ironhollow, a valley where magic cannot cross its borders. When her date's name appears in a century-old prophecy and the woman is pulled through a rift into the realm of Vaelmoor, Oscar follows — discovering she herself is the 'cartographer of the covenant' foretold to reforge the broken pact between realms before the solstice. Betrayed by the very order that wrote the prophecy, Oscar learns the covenant was shattered deliberately by those who feared shared power; with a found family of exiles, she must choose between restoring the old law or forging a new justice outside it. In the end, she rewrites the covenant in her own hand, sealing the rifts at the cost of her maps' magic — and returns to Ironhollow no longer bound by it.
about_author: Edmund Underhill is the pen name of a former surveyor who spent a decade mapping remote mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write fantasy rooted in the geometry of borders and the people who live just beyond them.

chapters.title: The Valley That Refuses Magic
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She finishes a map of an unmapped realm from secondhand accounts while preparing for a first date with Wren, a visiting archivist. The valley's magic-dead border is established through small details: no charms work, no rifts open. Emotional beat: quiet longing for a world she can only draw.

chapters.title: A Name Written a Century Ago
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At dinner, Wren confesses she found her own name in a sealed prophecy book dated 1897, describing 'the archivist who crosses on the eve of the thaw.' That night, a rift opens above the table and takes her. Emotional beat: wonder curdling into terror.

chapters.title: What the Border Keeps Out
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Grieving and disbelieving, Oscar interrogates the valley elders, who admit the border was built to keep something out — or in. She finds the prophecy page copied in her own grandmother's handwriting. Emotional beat: betrayal by inheritance.

chapters.title: Crossing Without Permission
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Using a flawed map of her own making, Oscar forces herself through the border at a thin place, losing sensation in her left hand as payment. She lands in Vaelmoor's ash-fields. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Ash-Field Guide
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV (a hedge-witch exile). Bramble finds Oscar half-frozen and recognizes the mark of a covenant-bearer on her hand. She offers shelter among the Unsworn — exiles from both realms. Emotional beat: wary kindness.

chapters.title: The Unsworn
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. In a hidden waystation, Oscar meets the found family: Bramble, the disgraced knight Sef, and twin smugglers Ilo and Ryn. They explain the covenant between realms broke forty years ago, and rifts now devour the borders. Emotional beat: belonging she never expected.

chapters.title: Where They Keep the Archivists
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. The group raids a Vaelmoor record-house where prophesied persons are detained. They find Wren alive but changed — she has been reading the full prophecy and refuses to leave until she understands her role. Emotional beat: rescue complicated by agency.

chapters.title: The Prophecy's Second Reader
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals the prophecy names two figures: the archivist who crosses, and the cartographer who redraws. It also names a betrayer within the company. Tension fractures the group's trust. Emotional beat: intimacy shadowed by suspicion.

chapters.title: Road Through the Riftlands
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. The company travels toward the Covenant Spire, navigating unstable rifts that erase geography. Oscar discovers her maps can stabilize ground — briefly. Emotional beat: competence becoming burden.

chapters.title: The Order of the Sealed Page
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Pursued by the Order that wrote the prophecy, the group learns the Order engineered the covenant's breaking to hoard magic for one realm. A skirmish costs them their supplies. Emotional beat: righteous anger hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Sef's Confession
chapters.summary: Sef's POV. Around the fire, Sef admits he was the knight who guarded the Spire when it fell — and that he let it fall, believing the old law unjust. The group must decide whether he is the betrayer. Emotional beat: shame met with grace.

chapters.title: The City of Borrowed Names
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The company passes through a free city where refugees from both realms live under assumed identities. Oscar sees what a new covenant could protect — and what the old one erased. Emotional beat: hope given a face.

chapters.title: What Wren Read Last
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren decodes the prophecy's final lines: the covenant can only be reforged by someone who belongs to neither realm — and the price is the bearer's anchor to home. Oscar realizes this means Ironhollow itself. Emotional beat: dread of sacrifice.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Glass Ford
chapters.summary: Bramble's POV. The Order ambushes the company at a river crossing. Bramble is gravely wounded holding the line; Oscar's map-magic saves them but burns out half her sight in one eye. Emotional beat: love proven in blood.

chapters.title: The Traitor Named
chapters.summary: Ilo's POV. The betrayer is revealed: not Sef, but Ryn, who has been feeding the Order their route since chapter six — trading loyalty for his twin's safety, held hostage. Emotional beat: heartbreak over villainy.

chapters.title: Two Brothers, One Rope
chapters.summary: Ryn's POV. Rather than punish him, the company plans to extract Ilo's leverage from the Order together. The rescue goes wrong; Ilo chooses capture so Ryn can escape with the group. Emotional beat: sacrifice inside family.

chapters.title: The Spire Beneath
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The remaining five reach the Covenant Spire, hollowed out and corrupted by the Order's seal. Oscar studies its architecture like a map and finds the original covenant was written to be rewritten — a design, not a decree. Emotional beat: revelation as liberation.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. On the eve of the deadline, the Order arrives in force with Ilo as hostage and demands the Spire be resealed under the old law. Negotiations collapse. Emotional beat: the last calm before the storm.

chapters.title: The Redrawing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Climax. As rifts tear open across both realms, Oscar draws a new covenant in her own hand — justice outside any law, binding realms by consent rather than decree. Wren anchors the words; Sef holds the line; Bramble bleeds for every stroke. Emotional beat: terrible, triumphant creation.

chapters.title: The Price of Ink
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The covenant seals, but the magic in Oscar's maps — and her tether to Ironhollow — burns away. Ilo is freed in the chaos; Ryn chooses to stay behind and rebuild the Spire's records honestly. Emotional beat: grief braided with peace.

chapters.title: Home, Unmapped
chapters.summary: Company POV, rotating. The group convalesces in the City of Borrowed Names, now openly itself. Wren and Oscar confront what they are to each other when the prophecy is fulfilled and neither is needed anymore. Emotional beat: love chosen freely.

chapters.title: Ironhollow Rising
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar returns to Ironhollow, which the new covenant has unsealed — magic seeps gently in for the first time in generations. She begins a new map: not of what is, but of what could be, with her found family beside her. Emotional beat: arrival, at last.
